direction: Evolve the static pairwise merge score as a globally depot-distance-normalized generalized savings rule: score(i,j) = (d0i + d0j - lam*dij + mu*|d0i-d0j|)/mean(d0[1:]) + beta*clip((q_i+q_j)/Q,0,1), with lam in [1.00,1.15], mu in [0.08,0.15], beta in [0.05,0.15]; forbid per-pair normalization by (d0i+d0j). Layer budgeted inter-route relocate + intra-route 2-opt postprocess on top of the evolved merge start to test residual gain of the construction layer (500 ms budget leaves large headroom: hook p50 sub-ms, full solve p95 ~10-12 ms at n=200).

operations.mechanism: KB verified that the L2a static hook with global depot-scale normalization is fast (<0.4 ms hook p50, p95 solve ~10-12 ms) and reaches dev_24 16.1398 / blind_120 24.2003 with postprocess_mode='none', beating bare CW (16.2225) and even CW+Relocate+2opt (16.1549). Timing headroom under the 500 ms budget is ~40x, so the open KB question — whether relocate_2opt on an evolved merge start retains residual gain — is affordable. Per-pair normalized savings is a documented antipattern (degrades dev_24 to ~18), so the round's search is constrained to the global-scale form while EoH tunes lam/mu/beta and the additive fill term.

preserve: Route feasibility, strict time budget, and scale invariance.
hypothesis: A single global depot-distance scale mean(d[0,1:]) preserves radial/remote-customer priority (hence 0.00% drift under 1e-3 coordinate scaling) and, with light edge-weight lam~1.0-1.15, radial asymmetry mu~0.08-0.15 and dimensionless fill bonus beta~0.05-0.15, gives a better merge sequence than bare Clarke-Wright; adding relocate_2opt on this evolved start yields further mean tour-length reduction on cvrp_dev_hetero_24 because the merge layer leaves capacity-feasible inter-route slack that local search can exploit (KB explicitly flags postprocess combination as an open question).
